For example, a normally exempt four-file Markdown PR becomes a five-file broad diff solely after its required acceptance record is written, causing the gate to demand an audit that the product changes themselves did not require; exclude this evidence path using the same normalized-path handling as `PR_FEEDBACK_EVIDENCE`.

items.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require a search command that actually scans the records**

The mandated substring accepts the passing fixture's `grep -l 'classes:…' .orchestration/learning/mistakes/`, but that command does not inspect files: on the repository's GNU grep it exits 2 with `Is a directory`, while `grep --help` identifies `-r, --recursive` as `like --directories=recurse`. Thus an acceptance record can satisfy S6 with a pasted search that returned no correction records; require recursive grep or a file glob and update the passing fixture accordingly.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind the grep pattern to the repeated class**

The class and grep checks are independent, so a record such as `search: scope: grep -l 'classes:.*x' .orchestration/learning/mistakes/*.md; contextdb_cli.py memory search x` passes: `slug.search(line)` finds `scope` in the prefix while `SEARCH_GREP.search(line)` accepts the unrelated `x` query. The gate therefore allows S6 evidence that never searches correction records for the repeated class; validate that the class token occurs inside the grep's `classes:` pattern. Fresh evidence in this head is the newly added compound condition, which still permits this bypass after the earlier bare-directory fix. The closed threat-table test does not cover this matching-prefix/wrong-query case.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Validate list-prefixed audit findings**

When an acceptance record formats a disposition as a Markdown list item, for example `- audit-finding: 1 … not-applicable:<reason>`, `str.strip()` leaves the `- ` prefix and this `startswith` check skips it. This is an existing record format (for example `.orchestration/acceptance/dotfiles-T65-agent-stop-gate-a01.md:41`), so with a `correct` audit verdict the merge gate accepts such a line without the newly required `evidence=` clause. Strip an optional Markdown list marker or match the disposition prefix explicitly; the closed acceptance-input threat-table test currently exercises only unprefixed lines.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject repeated evidence delimiters**

When a disposition contains multiple `; evidence=` delimiters, the greedy reason group splits at the last one. Consequently `not-applicable:; evidence=echo proof; evidence=true` is accepted with `; evidence=echo proof` as its supposedly non-empty reason, and a failure-level item can similarly pad a one-character reason past the 20-character minimum. This bypass affects PR feedback, audit dispositions, and acceptance-record validation through the shared regex; parse the first delimiter or explicitly reject additional delimiters. The closed acceptance-input threat-table test does not exercise this case.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require shell-command boundaries in pasted searches**

Because both command patterns are found as arbitrary substrings, a `search:` line containing `xgrep -l 'classes:.*scope' .orchestration/learning/mistakes/*.md; xcontextdb_cli.py memory search scope` passes `searches_class`, as does an `echo grep ...; echo contextdb_cli.py ...` line. In either case no required search command exists or scans the correction records, so a class repeated three times can still pass S6 with invalid pasted evidence. Require `grep` and `contextdb_cli.py` to begin actual shell command segments; the closed acceptance-input threat-table test does not cover this bypass.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Distinguish quoted grammar from a disposition**

When a fixed audit finding merely describes the `not-applicable:` syntax—for example, `audit-finding: 1 parser accepts not-applicable: without evidence -> fixed:abcdef0`—this substring check treats that mention as the line's disposition and rejects the task's acceptance record. This can block the mandatory integration gate for exactly the grammar-related findings this change addresses; identify the actual trailing disposition instead of using the first occurrence anywhere in the finding text. The closed acceptance-input test does not cover this case.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind the acceptance record to the current head**

After `gh pr update-branch` or any subsequent fix moves `HEAD`, an older acceptance record with the same task filename still passes this check because only its path and task name are validated. Even when the PR-feedback and audit inputs are refreshed for the new head, the stale record can omit newly introduced ledger rows or dispositions and thereby bypass the S6 check; require a machine-readable head binding and compare it with the current `HEAD` so the mandated sweep → audit → acceptance → gate order is enforceable.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Avoid quadratic backtracking in disposition parsing**

For a malformed disposition with no delimiter, or one containing a second `; evidence=`, the three overlapping repetitions in `DISPOSITION_PART` backtrack quadratically before rejecting it. In the reviewed environment, increasing a clause-less reason from 1,000 to 2,000 characters increased matching time from about 0.02s to 0.09s, and 5,000 characters took about 0.56s; several long malformed evidence entries can therefore stall the mandatory integration gate. Split once on the delimiter and validate the two parts with linear checks instead.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject duplicate acceptance-record keys**

`yaml.safe_load` silently keeps the last occurrence of a duplicate mapping key, so a record can visibly contain a three-row `ledger` followed by `ledger: []` (or two conflicting `head`/`pr` fields) and the gate validates only the latter value. This creates an ambiguous machine-versus-reviewer view and lets the S6 check be bypassed even though the record carries the repeated-class table. **<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind ledger rows to swept findings**

The S6 check counts only rows supplied by the acceptance record and never verifies that the ledger includes every item from `PR_FEEDBACK_EVIDENCE` or every audit finding. An acceptance record with `ledger: []`, or one that omits enough occurrences of a repeated class to keep its count below three, therefore passes and bypasses the mandatory records-search check. When the saved feedback changes or removes a Codex item's `author`, live recollection still accepts that item because `feedback_key()` does not compare `author`, but this filter then excludes it from the required ledger IDs.
